name: Phonikud Piper voices (Shaul, Michael) + Phonikud G2P
publisher: Phonikud (HF/GitHub org; code under thewh1teagle/phonikud); paper authors Yakov Kolani, Maxim Melichov, Cobi Calev, Morris Alper
publisher_note: Israeli open-source Hebrew G2P/TTS project run mainly by individual developers (org members include HF users thewh1teagle and notmax123); paper (Interspeech 2026, arXiv 2506.12311) lists Independent Researcher, Reichman Univ., Cisco, Tel Aviv Univ./CMU. Repo is non-commercial (CC-NC).
release_date_source: HF commit history: repo created 2025-05-28, first checkpoints uploaded 2025-06-02; Shaul ONNX 2025-06-16/17; Michael ONNX/ckpt 2026-03-24/25; arXiv paper v1 2025-06-14. Which voice the bakeoff uses decides the date.
architecture: Piper (VITS) with Phonikud IPA phonemes (stress + vocal shva)
params: Paper: Piper High 32M, Piper Medium 20M (ablations); checkpoints here are Lightning .ckpt ~846MB incl. discriminator
base_model: Paper: pre-trained English TTS checkpoint (unnamed). For the released Shaul/Michael checkpoints: not stated
training_origin: UNRESOLVED for released voices. Paper (sec 5.2) says Piper/StyleTTS2 were FINE-TUNED from pre-trained English checkpoints on 20 h of synthetic Hebrew audio (Gemini 2.5 Pro) with Phonikud IPA. Model card is empty, so whether Shaul/Michael were instead trained from scratch on SASPEECH is not confirmed. Not a confirmed Hebrew-only from-scratch model.
hebrew_training_data: Paper: 20 h synthetic Gemini 2.5 Pro audio. Related datasets in the org: SASPEECH (13+ h single speaker, openslr/134, non-commercial, with phonikud phonemes), ILSpeech (~2 h, studio, IPA-annotated). Checkpoint filenames (auto_phonemize_exp, 'shaul') suggest SASPEECH but this is inferred.
hebrew_input: Needs nikud/IPA: Phonikud G2P adds diacritics with an ONNX model (dictabert-char-menaked based) then rule FST -> IPA; plain Hebrew accepted through the pipeline
licence: Non-commercial (CC-NC) per model card; G2P code CC BY 4.0
confirmed: paper training method (fine-tune from English checkpoints, synthetic data)
inferred: mapping paper recipe onto released Shaul/Michael checkpoints

name: Piper Hebrew noa (medium)
publisher_note: Individual open-source developer, author of Phonikud/Renikud org projects (inferred: Yakov Kolani, Phonikud first author; GitHub profile shows no real name).
architecture: Piper VITS medium, 22.05 kHz ONNX, multi-speaker (noa + ljspeech)
params: not stated (Piper medium ~20M per Phonikud paper)
training_origin: fine-tuned for Hebrew from en_US-ljspeech-medium (which the card says was trained from scratch on LJSpeech). NOT Hebrew-only from scratch; Hebrew voice is trained on synthetic audio
hebrew_training_data: 24 h of Hebrew speech GENERATED WITH CHATTERBOX from Knesset sentences, Whisper-filtered (noa), plus ~24 h LJSpeech (English speaker). 20,322 steps. Code: github.com/thewh1teagle/piper-tts-finetune
hebrew_input: plain Hebrew; Piper phoneme_type 'hebrew' converts to stressed IPA via renikud (no manual nikud)

name: Kokoro Hebrew NC (he_shaul)
publisher: thewh1teagle (ONNX export); original model by avris (avris/kokoro-hebrew-saspeech, gated)
publisher_note: Conversion by an individual developer; the trained model is a third-party individual's (avris, no profile info). Non-commercial because derived from SASPEECH (Israeli Public Broadcasting Corp. data).
release_date_source: HF createdAt of this ONNX repo; source model avris/kokoro-hebrew-saspeech created 2026-06-30
training_origin: fine-tuned for Hebrew from Kokoro-82M (two-stage, StyleTTS2 trainer 'kikiri'). Not from scratch
hebrew_training_data: SASPEECH (openslr/134): stage 1 ~20 h automatic subset (from ~26 h, machine-vocalized with phonikud diacritizer), stage 2 ~4 h gold human-vocalized subset; single speaker Shaul Amsterdamski
hebrew_input: Phonikud G2P (needs/adds nikud) -> IPA normalised to Kokoro's 178-token vocab
confirmed: training recipe (read from gated avris card via page fetch)
inferred: release date of original beyond HF createdAt

name: BlueV3 (BlueTTS) v3.0.1
publisher: notmax123 = Maxim Melichov (HF fullname 'Maxim Melichov'; code github.com/maxmelichov/BlueTTS, site bluetts.com)
publisher_note: Israeli independent developer; HF org memberships include Kohn-AI (Kohn AI Consulting), Phonikud, Renikud, Yiddish-AI; co-author of the Phonikud paper (affil. Reichman University). Not listed as a public member of ivrit.ai.
release_date_source: HF commits: v3.0.0 2026-11-14, v3.0.1 (checkpoint 702000) 2026-11-15. Repo itself created 2026-07-11 (earlier v1.7.3 releases); BlueTTS GitHub repo created 2026-02-27
architecture: Flow-matching text-to-latent TTS with duration predictor and audio autoencoder (blue-codec); SupertonicTTS-style; zero-shot voice cloning; FlowTTS-GRPO RL post-training
params: '64M layout' for T2L per training README (inferred total small, tens of millions)
training_origin: trained from scratch, multilingual incl. Hebrew (7 languages: he, en, de, es, it, ru, yi); no base model named. Plus RL stage
hebrew_training_data: not stated on card. Voices are LibriTTS-R speakers (CC BY 4.0), i.e. English reference voices speaking Hebrew
hebrew_input: plain Hebrew; G2P RenikudPlus (ONNX, bundled) handles vowels/stress; numbers expanded; <en>..</en> for inline English
confirmed: ivrit.ai hosts 'Blue V2' Space (ivrit-ai/BlueV2, created 2026-04-28, commits by notmax123, README says duplicated from thewh1teagle/lightblue-tts-hebrew and points to notmax123/BlueV2) and lists it in its Hebrew TTS Arena as an open model
inferred: notmax123 == maxmelichov (same name 'Maxim Melichov' on HF and GitHub, BlueTTS logo 'by Maxim Melichov')
no formal ivrit.ai affiliation found: ivrit.ai merely hosts the V2 demo Space and arena entry; notmax123 has write access to that Space. V3 not confirmed as in the arena
